title: The Town and Country Planning (Discharge of Local Planning Authority Functions) (England) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations require relevant local planning authorities (“LPAs”) in England (as defined by section 319ZZF(1) of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (c. 8) (“TCPA 1990”)) to make arrangements for specified planning functions to be discharged by committees (including sub-committees) or by officers.

title: The Offshore (Oil and Gas) Installation and Pipeline Abandonment Charges (Revocation) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations introduce charges for or in connection with the carrying out by the Secretary of State of the Secretary of State’s functions under Part 4 of the Petroleum Act 1998 (c. 17) (“the 1998 Act”).

title: The Health and Social Care Act 2012 (Commencement No. 12) Order 2026
summary: This Order brings into force section 208 of the Health and Social Care Act 2012 (c. 7) (“the Act”) in so far as it is not already in force. It is the twelfth such Order to be made under the Act.

title: The Electricity Capacity (Amendment and Transitional Provision) Regulations 2026
summary: This instrument amends the Electricity Capacity Regulations 2014 (S.I. 2014/2043) (“the 2014 Regulations”), the Electricity Capacity (Supplier Payment etc) Regulations 2014 (S.I. 2014/3354) (“the Supplier Payment Regulations”) and the Electricity Capacity (No. 1) Regulations 2019 (S.I. 2019/862) (“the 2019 Regulations”).

title: The REACH (Amendment) (No. 2) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations amend the assimilated version of Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 concerning the Registration, Evaluation, Authorisation and Restriction of Chemicals (“the REACH Regulation”).

title: The Plugs and Sockets etc. (Safety) Regulations 1994 and Electricity Safety, Quality and Continuity Regulations 2002 (Amendment) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations amend the Plugs and Sockets etc. (Safety) Regulations 1994 (S.I. 1994/1768) and the Electricity Safety, Quality and Continuity Regulations 2002 (S.I. 2002/2665).

title: The National Security Act 2023 (Designated Bodies) Regulations 2026
summary: Part 1 of the National Security Act 2023 (c. 32) (“the Act”) makes provision for designated bodies (including offences in relation to such bodies). Section 33A(1) provides that the Secretary of State may, by regulations, designate a body. Section 33A(4) provides that such regulations may amend the Act so as to insert a Schedule listing the bodies designated under section 33A. Section 33A(6) provides that the Secretary of State may include alternative names in the designation of a body if the Secretary of State believes the body is, or has been, operating wholly or partly under more than one name.

title: The Energy Act 2023 (Commencement No. 5, Saving Provisions) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations bring into force section 299(3) to (7) of the Energy Act 2023 (c. 52) (“the 2023 Act”). These are the fifth set of regulations commencing provisions of the 2023 Act.

title: The Warboys, Somersham and Pidley Internal Drainage Board (Reconstitution) Order 2026
summary: This Order confirms, with modifications, a Scheme submitted by the Environment Agency making provision for the reconstitution of the Warboys, Somersham and Pidley Internal Drainage Board so that the number of elected members is reduced from twenty-one to fifteen.

title: The Contracts for Difference (Definition of Eligible Generator) (Amendment) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations amend the Contracts for Difference (Definition of Eligible Generator) Regulations 2014 (S.I. 2014/2010) (the “Eligible Generator Regulations”).

title: The March and Euximoor Water Management Board Order 2026
summary: This Order confirms, with modifications, a Scheme submitted by the Environment Agency for the amalgamation of the Euximoor Internal Drainage District and the March East Internal Drainage District into one new internal drainage district (“the March and Euximoor Internal Drainage District”). The Euximoor Internal Drainage Board and the March East Internal Drainage Board are abolished and a new internal drainage board (“the March and Euximoor Water Management Board”) is constituted for the new internal drainage district.

title: The M25 Junction 10/A3 Wisley Interchange Development Consent (Amendment) Order 2026
The Access to the Countryside (Coastal Margin) (Silecroft to Silverdale) (No. 2) Order 2026
summary: This Order appoints the day on which the access preparation period ends in relation to land which is coastal margin as a result of the approval by the Secretary of State of proposals contained in the reports relating to coastal access along the long-distance route between Silecroft to Silverdale. Copies of the notices of approval are available at www.gov.uk and may also be obtained by writing to the Department, Food and Rural Affairs, Seacole Building, 2 Marsham Street, London SW1 4DF.

title: The Access to the Countryside (Coastal Margin) (Harwich to Shotley Gate) (No. 1) Order 2026
summary: This Order appoints the day on which the access preparation period ends in relation to land which is coastal margin as a result of the approval by the Secretary of State of proposals contained in reports relating to coastal access along the long-distance route between Harwich to Shotley Gate. Copies of the notices approval are available at www.gov.uk and may also be obtained by writing to the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs, Seacole Building, 2 Marsham Street, London SW1 4DF.

title: The Justification Decision (Generation of Power by the RR SMR) Regulations 2026
summary: By these Regulations the Secretary of State makes a justification decision using the powers in regulation 4 of the Justification Decision Power (Amendment) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019 (S.I. 2019/215) and in accordance with the Justification of Practices Involving Ionising Radiation Regulations 2004 (S.I. 2004/1769) (“the 2004 Regulations”). The 2004 Regulations lay down basic safety standards for the protection of the health of workers and the general public against the dangers arising from ionising radiation.

title: The Wireless Telegraphy Act 2006 (Directions to OFCOM) (Revocation) Order 2026
summary: This Order revokes the Wireless Telegraphy Act 2006 (Directions to OFCOM) Order 2010 (“2010 Order”), through which the Secretary of State gave a number of directions to the Office of Communications (“OFCOM”). The directions were to vary wireless telegraphy licences, to amend spectrum trading regulations to allow the trading of licences, to amend regulations setting charges for the grant of a licence and to make regulations to set the rules for an auction of licences to use frequencies. The purposes of the 2010 Order are served, and the 2010 Order is now redundant.

title: The Trade (Mobile Roaming) (Amendment) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations amend the Trade (Mobile Roaming) Regulations 2023 (S.I. 2023/214) (“the Roaming Regulations”). The Roaming Regulations limit the wholesale roaming rates chargeable to mobile phone service providers in certain countries or territories with which the United Kingdom has an international agreement.

title: The Criminal Justice Act 1988 (Offensive Weapons) (Amendment) (England and Wales) Order 2026
summary: This Order amends the description of the weapon sometimes known as a “ninja sword” which is a prohibited weapon listed at paragraph 1(u) of the Schedule to the Criminal Justice Act 1988 (Offensive Weapons) Order 1988 (S.I. 1988/2019).

title: The Nuclear Safeguards (EU Exit and Fees) (Amendment) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations amend the Nuclear Safeguards (EU Exit) Regulations 2019 (S.I. 2019/196) (the 2019 Regulations) and the Nuclear Safeguards (Fees) Regulations 2021 (S.I. 2021/1406) (the 2021 Regulations). The 2019 Regulations require operators of qualifying nuclear facilities (as defined in section 76A(6) of the Energy Act 2013 (c. 32)) to maintain a system of accountancy and control of qualifying nuclear material, record and report specified information to the Office for Nuclear Regulation (the ONR) and/or the Secretary of State, and enable the ONR to verify compliance. The 2021 Regulations prescribe the fees payable by operators to the ONR for the costs incurred in exercising its functions under the 2019 Regulations (among other things).

title: The Bus Services Act 2025 (Commencement No. 2 and Transitional Provisions) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations bring into force specified provisions of the Bus Services Act 2025 (c. 24) (“the 2025 Act”). These are the second commencement regulations made under the 2025 Act.
